Verdict: REVISEThe substantive geometry, charge calculations, doubled-ledger correction, residual-capacity rule, and mixed-family arithmetic are correct under the intended channel hypotheses. I found no in-hypothesis counterexample to the freezing construction, the receiver counts, the sharp whole phase, the ownership argument, the  $-2B_E$  tax, or the stated mixed family.There is, however, one necessary scope repair in Section 3. As written, the section first quantifies over “a union  $C$  of complete physical squares,” but the transition-band conclusion
$$\Gamma_C(H)\ge 1$$
is only valid when  $C$  is an admissible rectangular region whose relevant extreme rows are endpoint-free, so that every transition endpoint path met by  $C$  is contained in full. The shifted partition must also trim the appropriate endpoint-free rows for the vertical shift. Without that condition, a region can cut the transition path, and the full transition-band calculation no longer applies.A precise replacement would be:For the horizontal shift, let  $C$  be an admissible rectangular union of complete physical squares with endpoint-free extreme columns, and retain only complete row bands. For the vertical shift, let  $C$  be an admissible rectangular union with endpoint-free extreme rows, and trim those rows in the shifted partition. Require that every endpoint path encountered in a listed band lies wholly inside  $C$ . Under these hypotheses the following band formulas hold.Then (5) should read:
$$\Gamma_C(H)\ge 0,$$
and
$$\Gamma_C(H)\ge 1$$
whenever  $C$  meets the full transition-band endpoint path.The stated tip-free rectangle
$$\{-2,\ldots,h+1\}\times\{w-3,w-2\}$$
does satisfy this repaired hypothesis, so its credit remains valid.1. All-parameter freezingThe freezing proof is sound for every even  $w\ge 6$  and  $h\ge4$ , including the edge case  $h=4$ .The two initial seeds are valid: $L=(2,0)$  sees  $(2,-1)$  and  $(3,0)$ ; $R_h=(h,w-1)$  sees  $(h,w)$  and  $(h+1,w-1)$ .The downward wave freezes the even  $R_r$ 's because  $R_r$  sees its retained outer support and  $R_{r+1}$ , whose mate  $R_{r+2}$  is already frozen.The chamber waves are also valid: $T_0$  is frozen from  $(0,-1)$  and the mate  $B_0$  of  $L$ ;the left wave freezes
$$T_{2i}\longrightarrow B_{2i+1}\longrightarrow T_{2i+2};$$
the reflected right wave starts from  $T_{w-1}$  and freezes  $B_{w-2}$ , then alternates back across the chamber;the remaining corners  $B_0$  and  $B_{w-1}$  are then frozen from mates of already frozen endpoints.The leg argument is likewise complete. The odd  $A_r=(r,w-2)$  endpoints are frozen from their retained inner support and the mate  $R_r$  of  $R_{r+1}$ . Then  $A_2$  is frozen from the two chamber mates, and the zigzag
$$A_4,R_5,A_6,R_7,\ldots$$
completes the lower leg. For  $h=4$ , the two seeds  $A_2,A_3$  and the resulting  $R_3$  already finish the leg; there is no missing intermediate step.Thus every endpoint in  $H$  has a valid finite frozen certificate. Additional feasible exterior selections do not undo a certificate, because all retained supports remain selected and the frozen-exclusion rule is monotone in the retained occupied-neighbor data.The proof does rely on the stated feasibility convention: a retained selected site may not acquire two occupied neighbors in the relevant promotion configuration. That convention should remain explicit when the geometric proof is separated from the abstract freezing lemma.2. Arbitrary feasible-exterior receiver labelsThe physical receiver count is correct:
$$|H|=2w+2h-2,
\qquad
|H|/2=w+h-1,$$
and the number of physical endpoint squares is
$$|R_H|=\frac w2+h+1.$$
The retained selected sites in those receiver squares number
$$|T\cap R_H|=h+4.$$
Therefore
$$\rho_H
=
|T\cap R_H|+\frac{|H|}{2}-2|R_H|
=
(h+4)+(w+h-1)-2\left(\frac w2+h+1\right)
=1.$$
The count is independent of the feasible exterior under the stated hypotheses.The corner argument is also valid. Every nonendpoint corner of a physical endpoint square is either:adjacent to enough  $H$ -endpoints to violate the feasibility condition if occupied; oradjacent to a retained support that already sees its prescribed endpoint, so occupying the corner would give that support an additional forbidden occupied neighbor.For shifted endpoint squares, two endpoints from distinct components could only occur at opposite corners. The retained support in the singleton occurrence blocks that possibility, while adjacent endpoint pairs necessarily belong to the same endpoint component. Thus a shifted endpoint square has a unique component owner as well.The one point that should be made explicit in the prose is that “foreign opposite-corner endpoints are excluded” uses the same occupied-neighbor feasibility rule as the freezing argument. Under that inherited convention, the ownership claim is correct.3. Partial-band tablesHorizontal shiftThe horizontal calculation is correct for admissible rectangles with endpoint-free extreme columns and complete physical row bands.The chamber and full-leg portions have zero raw excess in both phases. Each genuine physical tip contributes
$$+\frac12$$
in the physical partition and
$$-\frac12$$
in the shifted partition, hence contributes one unit to  $\Gamma_C(H)$ . Therefore
$$\Gamma_C(H)
=
\#\{\text{actual physical tip tiles of }H\text{ contained in }C\}.$$
The two paths in the  $\{2,3\}$  band do not create an extra term: the short left tip and the right leg path are disconnected, and the endpoint-free side condition prevents a partial horizontal path from being cut at a lateral boundary.Vertical shiftThe table is internally consistent:
$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{column band}
& \text{physical raw}
& \text{shifted raw}
& \text{gain}\\
\hline
\{-1,0\}
& \frac12
&-\frac12+a_0
&1-a_0\\
\{j,j+1\}
&0
&-2+a_j+b_j
&2-a_j-b_j\\
\{w-3,w-2\}
&0
&-2+a_\ast
&2-a_\ast\\
\{w-1,w\}
&\frac12
&-\frac12+a_{\mathrm{end}}
&1-a_{\mathrm{end}}
\end{array}$$
The transition calculation is:
$$(a_\ast-1)
+\left(-\frac12\right)
+0
+\left(-\frac12\right)
=
a_\ast-2.$$
Hence the transition gain is
$$0-(a_\ast-2)=2-a_\ast\ge1,$$
because  $a_\ast\in\{0,1\}$ . This remains valid for  $h=4$ ; there are simply no intermediate leg squares.The tip-free transition rectangle contains no physical tip tile but still earns at least one unit precisely because the junction and bottom-cap terms are present.The required revision is that the proof must explicitly say why those terms are present: the region must have endpoint-free extreme rows and must contain the entire connected transition path. If the path is cut through an interior boundary, one or both cap/junction terms disappear and the  $a_\ast-2$  sum is no longer available. Thus the transition credit is not a statement about arbitrary partial unions of physical squares.4. Sharp whole phaseThe whole vertical phase identity is correct:
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}(H)=w-A-B.$$
The upper-flank selections satisfy
$$A\le \frac w2,$$
because the  $w$  sites  $(-1,0),\ldots,(-1,w-1)$  form a path and each adjacent pair contains at most one selected site.For the lower flank,  $(2,1)$  cannot be selected because it sees the two  $H$ -endpoints  $(2,0)$  and  $(1,1)$ . Pairing the remaining sites gives
$$B\le \frac{w-4}{2}.$$
Consequently,
$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}(H)
\ge
w-\frac w2-\frac{w-4}{2}
=2.$$
The proposed selections
$$(-1,j),\qquad j=0,2,\ldots,w-2,$$
and
$$(2,j),\qquad j=2,4,\ldots,w-4,$$
are feasible for every  $w\ge6$ , and attain
$$A=\frac w2,
\qquad
B=\frac{w-4}{2},
\qquad
\Gamma_{\mathrm{full}}(H)=2.$$
Thus the constant two is sharp.5. Unique raw-square ownershipThe ownership argument is correct under the complete-component and feasibility hypotheses.Two distinct endpoint components cannot contribute adjacent endpoints to one square, since adjacent endpoints would be connected in the endpoint graph. The only possible distinct-component configuration is therefore a pair of opposite corners.For a singleton occurrence, the retained support in that square is adjacent both to the prescribed endpoint and to the opposite corner. Since that support already sees its own endpoint, the foreign opposite-corner endpoint is forbidden by feasibility. This applies in both the physical and shifted partitions.Thus the raw endpoint excess can be decomposed by component without counting the same endpoint square twice.6. The doubled ledger and the  $-2B_E$  taxThe extra-source tax is exactly correct.With  $B_L$  old long sources and  $B_E$  added elbows, the whole receiver ledger is
$$\Delta=-B_L-B_E+D_{\mathrm{all}}+E.$$
Doubling gives
$$2\Delta=-2B_L-2B_E+2D_{\mathrm{all}}+2E.$$
The old strip identity and physical donor incidence give
$$2D_{\mathrm{all}}
=
2B_L+F+A+D'+D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R_{\mathrm{noP}}.$$
With
$$R=R_{\mathrm{noP}}+E,$$
substitution yields
$$2\Delta
=
F+A+D'+D_{\mathrm{single}}+2R-2B_E.$$
Each elbow has whole corrected charge  $\rho_H=1$ , so its contribution to the doubled ledger is exactly  $-2$ . The tax does not depend on where the elbow’s phase is encountered in the strip or channel decomposition.Therefore omitting  $-2B_E$  is a genuine ledger error. It produces an overoptimistic certificate by exactly two doubled units per added elbow. It is not a counterexample to the global target; it is an invalid local allocation rule.7. Residual donor capacityThe capacity formula is correct. For a positive physical no-endpoint square  $Q$ , put
$$d_Q=2-|T\cap Q|.$$
If the original mouth strips cover  $Q$  with multiplicity  $m_Q\in\{0,1,2\}$ , the doubled ledger has total raw capacity  $2d_Q$ . The mouth calculation consumes  $m_Qd_Q$ , leaving
$$(2-m_Q)d_Q.$$
Consequently, channel weights must satisfy the pointwise condition
$$\sum_{j:Q\in C_j}w_j\le 2-m_Q$$
on every positive physical donor  $Q$ .This correctly prevents:using a donor once in the original mouth and twice in a channel;using the same channel certificate twice;treating phase gain as a second physical donor account.The channel phase and the mouth phase both certify the same physical deficit. They cannot be counted again as independent supply.8. Mixed all-parameter familyThe mixed construction is arithmetically correct.The physical channel contains
$$6(\ell+1)$$
squares. The elbow contributes  $h+4$  endpoint squares, so the no-endpoint count is
$$6(\ell+1)-(h+4)=6\ell-h+2.$$
The no-endpoint selected count is
$$12+2(\ell-1)+\delta
=
2\ell+10+\delta.$$
Therefore
$$D_C
=
2(6\ell-h+2)-(2\ell+10+\delta)
=
10\ell-2h-6-\delta.$$
For the trimmed shifted partition, the total number of squares is
$$5(\ell+1),$$
and the elbow occupies  $h/2+4$  endpoint squares. Hence the no-endpoint count is
$$5(\ell+1)-\left(\frac h2+4\right)
=
5\ell+1-\frac h2.$$
The shifted no-endpoint selected count is
$$10+(h+2)=h+12,$$
so
$$D'_C
=
2\left(5\ell+1-\frac h2\right)-(h+12)
=
10\ell-2h-10.$$
The difference is
$$D_C-D'_C=4-\delta.$$
Since the elbow is contained and parallel, its channel phase is  $2$ , and the channel boundary term is  $2-\delta$ . Thus
$$4-\delta=(2-\delta)+2,$$
exactly as required by the channel identity.With
$$F=-2,\qquad B_E=1,$$
and weight two, equation (8) gives
$$2\Delta
\ge
-2-2+2(2-\delta+2)
=
4-2\delta.$$
Therefore:if  $\delta=0$ , then  $\Delta\ge2$ ;if  $\delta=1$ , then  $\Delta\ge1$ .The assumption that all positive channel donors lie outside the zero-payment mouth is supported by the construction: the twelve first-band mouth selections occur in squares with two selections, hence zero donor deficit, while the remaining positive donors have original mouth multiplicity  $m_Q=0$ . This point should remain stated explicitly because it is what permits weight two.The omission of the horizontal comb blocker is also harmless: it removes a separate complete comb while leaving the root source, wall supports, mouth filling, and  $F=-2$  data unchanged. That independence should be said explicitly when the mixed family is presented outside the dependency note.9. Invalid local allocations versus the global targetThe following local rules are invalid:Reusing the old doubled ledger after adding elbows without subtracting  $-2B_E$ .Treating every elbow contact as two units of available donor supply.Assigning weight two to overlapping channels when a donor already has  $m_Q=1$ .Treating a tip-free transition contact as though it automatically paid two units; its guaranteed gain is only one.Counting shifted phase terms as additional donors after the physical donor deficit has already been allocated.Those failures do not refute the global coefficient-one target. They only invalidate the corresponding certificate or allocation rule. The valid theorem remains conditional on:the complete frozen endpoint data;the admissible rectangular channel geometry;the endpoint-free boundary conditions needed by the partial-band tables;the pointwise residual-capacity inequalities;the separate nonpositive-receiver coverage hypothesis;the existence of enough channels with the required signed-flux properties.After the Section 3 scope correction is made explicit, I would accept the mathematical content of the note.
